On some endpoints, Synapse will accept extraneous (suffix) data on the path of some endpoints.

When Synapse is protected by a reverse proxy (such as Nginx) and the reverse proxy normalises paths when routing (e.g. by converting `/a/../b` to `/b` for routing purposes), this can lead to a bypass of reverse proxy rules, allowing unintended endpoints to be exposed.
 
This constitutes a loss of defence in depth, and should not be directly exploitable, due to sensitive endpoints, such as Admin APIs, needing a valid access token for use.

### Patches

Update to Synapse 1.157.2 or later.

See the table below for patched versions of [Element Server Suite](https://element.io/en/server-suite), including Long-Term Support (LTS) versions.
|  | 25.10 LTS | 26.4 LTS | Latest |
|:--|--|--|--|
| **ESS Pro** | `25.10.14+lts` | `26.4.9+lts` | `26.7.2` |
| **ESS Classic** | `25.10.09-gui` | `26.04.04-gui` | ⸻ |
| **ESS Community** | ⸻ | ⸻ | `26.7.2` |
| **ESS TI-Messenger** | `25.10.10` | `26.4.5` | `26.7.0` |

### Workarounds

- Configure your reverse proxy not to use normalised paths for routing purposes. (i.e. `/a/../b` should be treated as a subpath of `/a`, not of `/b`)
- If applicable, avoid relying on reverse proxy rules alone to protect sensitive endpoints; instead [configure multiple listeners](https://element-hq.github.io/synapse/v1.157/usage/configuration/config_documentation.html?highlight=resources#listeners) and segregate sensitive endpoints onto their own port that way.

### Identifiers

-   ELEMENTSEC-2026-1760

### For more information
